metadata.corpus_name: Critical Minerals OSINT Demo Corpus - 2026 Developments
metadata.scope: Curated 2026 OSINT developments for five critical-minerals project nodes.
metadata.demo_disclaimer: Sources are manually curated for demonstration. Priority labels and relevance scores are demo ranking outputs, not independently validated quantitative risk scores.
metadata.ranking_intent: Prioritize developments that materially change ownership/control, production status, capacity, financing/offtake, operational state, or geopolitical exposure of the node.

nodes.node_name: Browns Range Heavy Rare Earths Project

articles.title: Federal treasurer orders more Chinese-linked investors to offload shares in Australian rare earths mine
articles.what_changed: Australia's Treasurer ordered six China-linked investors holding roughly 17% of Northern Minerals to divest their stakes.
articles.summary: The Australian government escalated scrutiny of Northern Minerals' shareholder base by issuing new divestment orders on national-interest grounds.
articles.why_it_matters: Northern Minerals owns and is developing Browns Range. A forced change in a large block of ownership can affect governance, financing, strategic control, and the development trajectory of a project intended to supply dysprosium and terbium outside China.

articles.title: China-linked investors' refusal to divest from WA heavy rare earths company 'extraordinary', expert says
articles.what_changed: The investors subject to the May divestment order had not fully complied by the deadline and still held a majority of the shares they had been directed to sell.
articles.summary: The ownership dispute surrounding Northern Minerals remained unresolved after the federal divestment deadline, raising the prospect of further government enforcement.
articles.why_it_matters: This is an escalation of an unresolved ownership and control risk around the company developing Browns Range, rather than a one-off policy announcement. It is the type of follow-on development a continuous monitoring system should elevate.

articles.title: USA Rare Earth Announces Definitive Agreement to Acquire Serra Verde Group for ~$2.8 Billion
articles.what_changed: USA Rare Earth announced a definitive agreement to acquire Serra Verde for an implied value of about $2.8 billion.
articles.summary: The transaction would combine Serra Verde's producing heavy-rare-earth operation with USA Rare Earth's downstream processing, metallization, and magnet-manufacturing capabilities.
articles.why_it_matters: A change of control at a producing heavy-rare-earth operation can alter downstream flows, strategic alignment, capital availability, and integration into U.S.-linked magnet supply chains.

articles.title: USA Rare Earth Announces Completion of Upsized $1.55 Billion Capitalization of the U.S. Government-Backed SPV for Serra Verde Offtake
articles.what_changed: The special-purpose vehicle intended to purchase Serra Verde Phase 1 production completed an upsized $1.55 billion capitalization package, including U.S. government support.
articles.summary: The financing and forward-purchase structure strengthened the economic and strategic support surrounding Serra Verde's production and 15-year offtake arrangement.
articles.why_it_matters: Long-term offtake, price floors, and government-backed capitalization can reduce demand and price risk for the operation while tying its output more directly to U.S. strategic supply-chain objectives.

articles.title: USA Rare Earth Completes Combination with Serra Verde Group
articles.what_changed: USA Rare Earth completed its combination with Serra Verde on September 3, 2026.
articles.summary: The previously announced transaction closed, formally placing Serra Verde within an integrated mine-to-magnet rare-earth platform.
articles.why_it_matters: This converts a proposed ownership change into an executed one. For current-state monitoring, the closing should outrank the earlier acquisition announcement because it changes the actual ownership and strategic context of the node.

articles.title: MP Materials Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026
articles.what_changed: MP Materials stated in its Q2 2026 Form 10-Q that it expects to begin heavy-rare-earth refining in the second half of 2026, with initial production of terbium and dysprosium.
articles.summary: MP Materials said it expects to begin refining heavy rare earth elements at Mountain Pass in the second half of 2026, starting with terbium and dysprosium.
articles.why_it_matters: Beginning domestic terbium and dysprosium refining would expand what the Mountain Pass node can supply and reduce reliance on external heavy-rare-earth processing. This is a change in processing capability, not merely a production-volume update.

articles.title: MP Materials Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026
articles.what_changed: MP disclosed plans to extend heavy-rare-earth refining to samarium oxide and add scaled magnet-recycling capacity at Mountain Pass with dedicated NdPr and heavy-rare-earth separation.
articles.summary: The company is broadening Mountain Pass from mining and separation into a more flexible feedstock and recycling hub.
articles.why_it_matters: Recycling and additional HREE separation diversify feedstock and product pathways at the node, potentially increasing resilience and altering future material flows through the U.S. rare-earth supply chain.

nodes.node_name: Mt Weld Mine and Concentration Plant

articles.title: Lynas Rare Earths Limited - Annual Report 2026
articles.what_changed: Lynas reported completion of construction and commissioning for the Mt Weld expansion, with the new flowsheet continuing to ramp during FY2026.
articles.summary: The expansion moved from construction into operational ramp-up, while Lynas also reported water-recycling and ore-variation challenges that affected downstream processing.
articles.why_it_matters: This directly changes the productive state and expected throughput of Mt Weld. The reported ramp-up issues are also material operational signals because they affected concentrate quality and downstream productivity.

articles.title: Lynas Rare Earths FY26 Half Year Results
articles.source: Lynas Rare Earths / ASX market announcement
articles.what_changed: Lynas reported that commissioning of the Mt Weld expansion was complete and the new flotation circuit had ramped to about 70% of nameplate.
articles.summary: The half-year update provided an earlier 2026 milestone showing the expansion transitioning into production optimization and recovery improvement.
articles.why_it_matters: This establishes the trajectory leading into the later FY2026 ramp-up update and gives the system temporal context for whether Mt Weld is progressing, stalling, or encountering new operational constraints.

articles.title: Lindian completes first blast at Kangankunde, starts active mining
articles.what_changed: Kangankunde completed its first production blast, marking the start of active mining operations.
articles.summary: The project moved from development/construction into active mining, with ore being hauled to run-of-mine stockpiles ahead of process-plant commissioning.
articles.why_it_matters: This is a true state transition for the node. A project moving from construction to active mining materially changes its readiness, schedule risk, and expected timing of future rare-earth supply.

articles.title: Lindian says Kangankunde on track for production this year
articles.what_changed: Lindian reported that Kangankunde remained on track for Q4 2026 first production, with mining, stockpiling, plant construction, and power infrastructure advancing.
articles.summary: The update provided evidence that the July transition into mining was being followed by continued progress toward commissioning and first production.
articles.why_it_matters: For a developing mine, schedule execution is a key strategic variable. This follow-on update helps distinguish a one-time construction milestone from sustained progress toward becoming an operating supply source.
